 1. Read-Through Cache
💡 Idea
👉 Application always reads from cache first

✅ Flow
User → App → Cache
             ↓
         Hit ✅ → return
             ↓
         Miss ❌ → DB → store in cache → return


✅ Example: User Profile
🔸 First request (Cache Miss)
getUser(101)
→ Cache (not found ❌)
→ DB → fetch user data
→ Store in cache
→ Return response


🔸 Second request (Cache Hit)
getUser(101)
→ Cache ✅ (fast)
→ Return directly


✅ Code-style example
function getUser(id) {
    data = cache.get(id)
    
    if (data == null) {
        data = db.get(id)
        cache.set(id, data)
    }
    
    return data
}


✅ Use case

Most common ✅
Read-heavy systems


✅ 🔷 2. Write-Through Cache
💡 Idea
👉 Whenever you update data → update both Cache + DB together

✅ Flow
User → App → Cache (update)
               ↓
            DB (update)


✅ Example: Update User Name
updateUser(101, "Bikash")
→ Update Cache ✅
→ Update DB ✅


✅ Code-style example
function updateUser(id, data) {
    db.update(id, data)
    cache.set(id, data)
}


✅ Benefit
✅ Cache always stays consistent with DB

❌ Downside

Slightly slower writes
More operations


✅ 🔷 3. Write-Back (Write-Behind)
💡 Idea
👉 Write to cache first → DB updated later (async)

✅ Flow
User → App → Cache (update)
               ↓
        Queue / Worker
               ↓
             DB (later)


✅ Example: Like Button (Instagram)
likePost(101)
→ Cache increment ✅ (fast)
→ Queue event
→ DB updated later (async)


✅ Code-style concept
function likePost(id) {
    cache.increment(id)
    queue.push(id)   // async DB update later
}


✅ Benefit
✅ Extremely fast writes
✅ Good for high traffic

❌ Risk

Data mismatch if crash
DB delay


🔥 🔷 Comparison (Interview Gold)

Read-Through: Cache-first read, DB on miss, fast reads, medium consistency
Write-Through: Update cache + DB together, safe, strong consistency
Write-Back: Write to cache first, DB async, very fast, risk of inconsistency

🔷 Real-Life Mapping
Use Case			Strategy
User profile		Read-Through
Banking data		Write-Through
Likes / counters	Write-Back


✅ ✅ Interview Answer (Perfect)

“In read-through caching, the application first checks the cache and fetches from 
the database on a miss. In write-through, updates are written to both cache and database simultaneously
 to maintain consistency. In write-back, data is written to cache first and asynchronously persisted 
 to the database, improving performance but introducing eventual consistency.”
